objective: Find out how Billion Context (ranxianglei/billion-context, with its acp-kernel) can be installed for HolyAgent's pi integration, and what it requires.
scope: Maintainer (verbatim): "also billioncontext shall be installed". Context: HolyAgent's Claude plugin once depended on Billion Context to compress the conversation and removed it in commit 85a8560 (PR #40, 2026-10-29; 'git show 85a8560' in /home/user/holyagent shows what it installed and the attribution text it carried). The pi plan is in /home/user/holyagent/docs/pi/.

Answer with dated links: does Billion Context support pi (a pi package or extension, an MCP server, or only Claude Code and other hosts); how it is installed and configured for pi; how it interacts with pi's own compaction and with prompt caching on Kimi for Coding; its current version, release cadence and maintenance; its license terms, including the visible attribution requirement quoted in that commit; its runtime needs (Node version, native modules) and Windows support; and whether it works with pi-subagents children and codemode.
constraints: Read-only: write no files and make no git writes; put the full answer in the report.
Keep working until done; stop and report. Report in under 400 words, a verdict line first.

criteria.text: Pi support, install route and license terms are answered from dated, linked sources or marked unknown

result:
**Verdict: Billion Context supports pi directly and can be installed, with the license text clean (plain MIT) but the old attribution requirement not re-checked. Several interaction questions (Kimi caching, codemode) are unknown.**

I could not run `git show 85a8560` because I have no shell, so I did not compare the quoted attribution text against the current terms.

**Pi support (dated sources)**
- The repo README lists pi as a supported client, via `bili pi` (launcher) or `bili plugin install pi` (native). The standalone `billion-context-pi` package also remains usable. [github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context), fetched 2026-11-07.
- It is also a pi package: the manifest declares extension `./dist/agent/pi-native.js`. `pi install npm:billion-context` is the pi route. [pi.dev/packages/billion-context](https://pi.dev/packages/billion-context): v0.1.212, published 2 Nov 2026, MIT, 45.3 MB.
- Two routes exist, and they are mutually exclusive (running both double-compresses):
  - Native: `bili plugin install pi`. Needs `npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local` first.
  - Standalone: `pi install npm:billion-context-pi`. It needs pi >= 0.83 and has zero runtime dependencies. [billion-context-pi README](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context-pi). The npmjs.com page for this package is dated 2026-09-30.

**Interaction with pi's compaction**
- The standalone extension cancels pi's auto-compaction with `session_before_compact` returning cancel. [billion-context-pi `src/index.ts`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context-pi/blob/2c460050/src/index.ts).
- I did not confirm the native route's compaction behavior. The README only says the opencode installer "disables native auto-compaction".

**Prompt caching and Kimi for Coding**
- Unknown for Kimi for Coding specifically.
- The README claims a 95-97% prefix-cache hit rate and "prefix-cache friendly" compression. This is the project's own claim, with no independent source.
- The pi-mono changelog says Kimi for Coding accepts tools added mid-conversation without invalidating the prompt cache. [pi-mono commit a3f265b](https://upd.dev/badlogic/pi-mono/commit/a3f265b1c6a49bc0904c76518d2d436ba44c95e9.diff). That matters because Billion Context injects its own tools.

**Version and maintenance**
- v0.1.212 was released 2 Nov 2026. v0.1.211 came 1 Nov and v0.1.210 on 31 Oct, so releases land roughly daily. [GitHub releases](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/releases)
- The repo was created 2026-08-06 and has 4333 stars and 884 open issues. One maintainer wrote about 3635 contributions.
- That is a very young project with a very high change rate. Pin the version.

**License**
- LICENSE on master is plain MIT, copyright (c) 2026 ranxianglei. `package.json` also says MIT. [LICENSE](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/blob/master/LICENSE)
- I found no visible-attribution requirement beyond MIT's copyright-notice clause.
- GitHub's sidebar says "Other", which conflicts with the MIT text. The v0.1.212 notes mention a PR titled "Manually remove the fucking AI restrictions", so the terms may have changed recently.
- Your quoted attribution text may therefore be stale. Compare it with the commit and re-check the LICENSE history.

**Runtime**
- Node >= 20. The one native module is `sharp`, and it is optional. The `acp-kernel` dependency is MIT-licensed and bundled.
- The README gives Windows install instructions, but I found no explicit Windows support statement for pi. Treat that as unverified.

**pi-subagents children and codemode**
- Billion Context ships its own `acp_delegate` subagent tools (`acp_delegate`, `acp_delegate_wait`, `acp_delegate_cancel`), on by default.
- With `pi-subagents` installed, the built-in delegate stands down. The README now says this applies at user or project scope (#5637); an older README said project scope only.
- `pi-subagents` children do not get compression unless you run `/acp-subagents` (standalone package) or set `delegate.forceEnable`.
- To keep compression but drop the built-in subagents, set `{"pi":{"subagents":false}}` in `~/.config/billion-context/billion-context.json`.
- I found nothing on codemode compatibility, so it is unknown.

evidence:
Pi support, install route and license terms are answered from dated, linked sources or marked unknown: pi support, install routes, version and cadence, MIT license and subagent behavior are linked above with dates. Unknown or unverified: the commit's attribution text, Kimi cache behavior, codemode, and Windows support for pi.
